headline: Markets steady into Thanksgiving as AI trade cautiously returns
body: Sentiment this week has been dominated by one company's whiplash. Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, November 23, just six days after chairman Harvey Jones told investors the board had no intention of bringing him back following Huang's abrupt November 12 resignation amid unconfirmed personal-conduct allegations. The reversal, reported to have come under pressure from the White House, sent Nvidia shares up roughly 31% in a single session — the largest one-day dollar gain on record for a US company — and lifted the S&P 500 4.7%, its best day since April 2025, with gains spreading across most major chipmakers. Even so, Nvidia remains about 30% below its October 6 peak, a reminder of how much ground the broader AI-correction selloff of early November, which saw the Nasdaq 100 post its worst single day since the 2020 crash, still has to recover.

Heading into the holiday, the tone has shifted from relief rally to cautious stabilization: reporting into Thursday describes European and Asian shares extending gains as investors tentatively return to AI names, even as commentary accompanying the move stressed that renewed conviction in the AI trade is still yet to come rather than confirmed. Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China exposure and chip-export compliance, plus lingering unease over debt-financed AI infrastructure spending, remain background risks that the week's bounce hasn't resolved. Wall Street itself is closed for Thanksgiving and faces only a shortened Friday session, thinning volumes further. Verified retail-sentiment chatter specific to today was hard to pin down amid the holiday lull, so this read leans more on price action and headline flow than on confirmed social-media positioning.
